chapter: Asides on character, a piano and Oslo
title: Louis Bergerer, the French pianist, and tracing him after the war
summary: A French pianist who worked with Briggs in 1923 later became a butter-company director; they found each other again through a friend who had seen Briggs at Chez Florence.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: The piano I have, at home.
This is a very nice grand piano that is in the living room.
Yes, that piano was sold to me -- I say "sold," it was almost given to me, by a pianist who worked with me way back in 1923, a Frenchman.
He became the manager and director of one of the biggest butter firms in France after. His name was Louis Bergerér.
He died while three years ago I was with him, not every day until his death, but I was with him most always.
Because we caught up with each other--
I'm a little nervous, I don't know why. 'Cause I haven't spoken like this --
Don't worry about it. We're just talking.
We caught up with each other, we found each other, it was an accident, through a friend. He, being manager-director of this big butter company -- what's the name of it -- Privado.

Privado Butter Company in France, and during the conversation he had with someone, they mentioned that they had seen at the Chez Florence Cabaret in Paris after liberation, because he, Bergerér, I think he managed to get -- he went to the States, he managed to get to New York before the Germans came in. And he said --'Chez Florence, I had a very good friend, I know he was at Chez Florence from 1946 on. His name was Arthur
